sentences.text:
The petitioners being accused Nos. 3 and 4 are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them by respondent pending in C.C.No.113/2016 (Old No.623/2014), on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Holalkere, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code ( in short IPC).
2. Brief facts of the case are that, respondent No.2 as informant filed the first information against accused Nos.1 to 4, alleging commission of the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
It is alleged in the first information that the informant married accused No.1 on 17.02.2010 and thereafter led marital life.
After few days, accused No.1 went to Maharashtra to pursue his studies and NC: 2024:KHC:32563 the informant started residing in the matrimonial house along with accused Nos.2 to 4.
After about a year, accused Nos.2 to 4 started abusing the informant in filthy language as she has not begotten any child and also assaulted her with hands.
About 2 months earlier to the first information, the informant came to her parental house and started residing there.
On 24.08.2013, the accused came to her parental house, abused in filthy language, assaulted her and gave life threat.
Therefore, she requested the police to register the case and to initiate legal action.
Accordingly, FIR in Crime No.615/2013 came to be registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.

Now it is stated that after investigation, charge sheet came to be filed and the matter is pending in C.C.No.113/2016 on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge & JMFC, Holalkere, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
3.
After filing the charge sheet, accused Nos. 3 and 4 have filed this petition for quashing criminal proceedings initiated against them.

sentences.text: 2 4. Heard Sri. Venkatesh T.S, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt. N. Anitha Girish, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri. R Shashidhara, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on records.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that accused No.1 married respondent No.2 on 17.02.2010 and they led marital life for sometime and filed MC.No.29/2013, seeking divorce by mutual consent.
Subsequently, the same came to be dismissed.
During pendency of MC.No.29/2013 accused No.1 filed MC No.63/2013 seeking divorce on the ground of desertion.
However, later it was withdrawn.
Learned counsel further submits that it is only after withdrawal of MC.No.63/2013, the present complaint came be to filed.
Bald and general allegations are made against these petitioners and there is no specific overt act against them.
Accused No.3 is the sister of accused No.1 and accused No.4 is husband of accused No.3.
They are residing separately in the address mentioned in the petition and they have nothing to do with the family affairs of accused No.1 and respondent No.2.
Only to harass the petitioners, the complaint was filed against them.

Even in NC:
2024:KHC:32563 MC.No.6/2015 filed by respondent No.2, seeking divorce, which was filed on 28.09.2015, respondent No.2 had not made any allegations against these petitioners.
Under such circumstances, initiation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners amounts to abuse of process of law.
Accordingly, he prays for allowing the petition.

6. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader and learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against the petitioners and accused Nos.1 and 2 for having committed the offence.
The informant specifically stated that the petitioners along with other accused abused her in filthy language, assaulted and gave her life threat.
When such specific allegations are made, the petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, pray for dismissal of the petition.

7. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioners have made out any grounds to allow the petition and NC:
2024:KHC:32563 to quash the criminal proceeding initiated against them?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 8.
The informant filed the first information alleging that she married accused No. 1 on 17.02.2010.
She stayed in the matrimonial house for sometime and came back to her parental house.
After coming back to her parental house, on 24.08.2013, the accused came to her house, abused her in filthy language, assaulted her and gave life threat.
It is pertinent to note that initially on 25.06.2013 accused No.1 and respondent No.2 had filed MC.No.29/2013, seeking divorce by mutual consent.
The same came to be dismissed.
During pendency of MC.No.29/2013, accused No.1 filed MC.No.63/2013, seeking divorce from respondent No.2 on the ground of desertion.

Subsequently,
the same came to be withdrawn.

In the meantime, the present first information came to be filed and Smt Anitha vs State By Holalkere Police Station on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103738688/
3 FIR came to be registered.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that during 2015, respondent No.2 filed MC.No.6/2015, seeking divorce where accused No.1 was placed ex-parte and it is stated that the petition is already allowed and divorce was granted.
However, it is the specific contention of the petitioners that no allegations were made against these petitioners in said petition MC.No.6/2015.
The same was not controverted by respondent No.2.
Admittedly, respondent No.2 has not sustained any injuries in the incident that had occurred.
It is stated that the petitioners are the permanents residents of the address mentioned in the petition and they have nothing to do with the family affairs of accused No.1 and respondent No.2.
It appears that since there was marital discord between accused No.1 and respondent No.2, it is an attempt to rope in all the family members, by making bald and general allegations.

10. Under these circumstance, I am of the opinion that there are no reasons to permit the criminal proceedings to continue against the petitioners as it would amount to infringement of the right of the petitioners and also abuse of the process of the Court.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.

( ii) Criminal proceedings initiated against accused Nos.
3 and 4 in C.C.No.113/2016 (Old No.623/2014), on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge & JMFC,
Holalkere, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
